_doc: How far the Harrison 1830 pre-cut reading sits from the derived 1812 shore. GENERATED by tools/measure_shore_1812_harrison.py from the two committed files named under `inputs`; do not hand-edit (check.sh re-measures it). It is a MEASUREMENT and changes no geometry: Wright 1834 carries shore_1812_pre_cut by the owner's ruling of 2026-09-17, and docs/RESEARCH/shore_1812_pre_cut.md section 6 says what these numbers mean and what they do not settle (T-1286).

method.targets: derived features of kind bar, shore, unmodelled_gap
method.no_counterpart: a station whose nearest derived point is the free end of a derived line is counted under `no_counterpart_m`, not measured
method.bins: distance from the transform's anchor (local E/N [1152.0, 221.0]), 100 m

evidence_sentence: The one pre-cut sheet held, Harrison's of February 1830 (unscaled, re-engraved in 1884), was measured against these lines (T-1286, data/terrain/1812_harrison_cross_check.json): within 100 m of the fort its banks sit a median 9 m and at most 31 m from them, but down the old southward channel, 200 m and more from the fort, they sit 120 m away at the median and up to 157 m, and it letters the old mouth 357 m north of the adopted station. That disagreement is filed, not resolved.

mouth.harrison_old_mouth_from: centre of the trace's declared `old_mouth` cut, where Harrison letters 'Old Mouth of River very shallow'
